chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan from Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his fathers (peace be upon them) who said:

key_terms.آكِلَ ثَمَنِهَا: The one who consumes its price

ai.seo_question: Who are the people cursed regarding wine in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Zayd ibn Ali expands the divine curse (*la'na*) beyond the consumer to encompass the entire economic and social chain of wine, including producers, sellers, and even those who consume its price. This comprehensive enumeration underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the prohibition is not merely ritualistic but affects all parties involved in the commodity's lifecycle, reinforcing the severity of *khamr* as a root of all vices.
